children: Basis bids for soybeans shipped by barge to the US Gulf Coast firmed on Tuesday, reflecting exporter demand as the US Department of Agriculture continued to confirm fresh soybean sales to China.
The USDA confirmed private sales of 612,000 metric tons of US soybeans to China under its daily reporting rules, the fifth sales announcement to China in as many business days.
Analysts noted market chatter of additional soybean purchases on Tuesday, as Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures (SX26) fell to their lowest level since late August.
An active harvest pace amid favorable Midwest weather in recent days steered more soybeans into marketing channels. Farmers were generally inclined to sell soybeans while storing corn, brokers said.
The USDA said the soybean harvest was 64% complete by Sunday, up from 46% the previous week, while the corn harvest was 44% finished, up from 33% previously.

At the Gulf, CIF soybean barges loaded in October were bid at 99 cents over Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) November soybean (SX26) futures, up 4 cents from Monday. Barges loaded in the last half of October traded at 104 cents over futures.

FOB export premiums for Gulf soybeans loaded in November held steady at around 120 cents over futures. Offers for first-half November loadings, at 117 cents over futures on Monday, were no longer quoted.

For corn, CIF corn barges loaded in October were bid at 83 cents over CBOT December corn (CZ26) futures, unchanged from Monday. November corn barges were bid at 90 cents over futures, up a penny from Monday.
FOB export premiums for Gulf corn vessels loaded in first-half November were around 98 cents over CBOT December futures, down 3 cents from Monday.
Barge freight costs eased, with empty barges on the Mississippi River at St. Louis for this week offered at 650% of tariff, down from 700% a day earlier.
River levels were declining in some locations due to dry Midwest weather, a barge source noted.
